sanskrit: vātāj jāto antarikṣād vidyuto jyotiṣas pari | sa no hiraṇyajāḥ śaṅkhaḥ kṛśanaḥ pātv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: Born from the wind, from the atmosphere, from the lightning, from the light — may that golden-born conch-shell, the kṛśana-gem, guard us from distress.

sanskrit: hiraṇyānām eko 'si somād adhi jajñiṣe | rathe 'si dārśata iṣudhau rocanas tvam ||
english: You are the chief among golden things; you were born from Soma. You are the radiant one in the chariot, luminous in the quiver.

sanskrit: yo agrato rocanāvān samudrād adhi jajñiṣe | śaṅkhena hatvā rakṣāṃsy atriṇo vi ṣahāmahe ||
english: You who, radiant in the front, were born from the ocean — by means of the conch-shell, having struck down the rākṣasas and the devourers, we overpower them.

sanskrit: ye atriṇo yātudhānā rakṣaso ye kimīdinaḥ | sarvāñ chaṅkha tvayā vayaṃ viṣūco vi ṣahāmahe ||
english: Those who are devourers, the sorcerers, the rākṣasas, those who are kimīdins — all of them, O conch-shell, by means of you we overpower in every direction.

sanskrit: śaṅkhenāmīvām amatiṃ śaṅkhenota sadānvāḥ | śaṅkho no viśvabheṣajaḥ kṛśanaḥ pātv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: With the conch-shell we drive away disease and wretchedness; with the conch-shell we also drive away the ever-gnawing ones. The conch-shell, the universal remedy, the kṛśana-gem — may it guard us from distress.

sanskrit: divi jātaḥ samudrataḥ sindhutas pary ābhṛtaḥ | sa no hiraṇyajāḥ śaṅkha āyuṣprataraṇo maṇiḥ ||
english: Born in heaven, brought from the ocean, fetched from the river — that golden-born conch-shell, the jewel that extends life, shall be ours.

sanskrit: devānām asthi kṛśanaṃ babhūva tad ātmanvac caraty apsv antaḥ | taṃ te badhnāmy āyuṣe varcasa ojase ca balāya ca kārśanas tvābhi rakṣatu ||
english: The kṛśana became the bone of the gods; endowed with vital essence it moves amid the waters. I bind it upon you for life, for radiance, for vigor, and for strength — may the kṛśana-gem guard you on all sides.

sanskrit: kanyā vār avāyatī somam api srutāvidat | astaṃ bharanty abravīd indrāya sunomi tvā śakrāya sunomi tvā ||
english: A maiden, going to fetch water, found Soma flowing beside it. While carrying it homeward she spoke: "For Indra I press you; for Śakra I press you."

sanskrit: asau ya eṣi vīrako gṛhaṃgṛhaṃ vicākaśat | imaṃ jambhasutaṃ piba dhānāvantaṃ karambhiṇam apūpavantam ukthinam ||
english: O you hero who goes about, peering into house after house — drink this Soma pressed by Jambha's mouth, accompanied by parched grain and gruel, with cakes, worthy of the uktha-hymn.

sanskrit: kuvic chakat kuvit karat kuvin no vasyasas karat | kuvit patidviṣo yatīr indreṇa saṃ gamāmahai ||
english: Will he perhaps be able? Will he perhaps act? Will he perhaps make us more prosperous? Will those women who hate their husbands come to unite with Indra?

sanskrit: ā cana tvā cikitsāmo 'dhi cana tvā nemasi | śanair iva śanakair iva- -indrāyendo pari srava ||
english: We do not even seek to cure you; we do not even press you hard. Gently, gently — O Indu, flow around for Indra.

sanskrit: imāni trīṇi viṣṭapā tānīndra vi rohaya | śiras tatasyorvarām ād idaṃ ma upodare ||
english: These three expanses, O Indra, cause to grow apart — the head of that man, the field, and this here upon my belly.

sanskrit: asau ca yā na urvarā- -ād imāṃ tanvaṃ mama | atho tatasya yac chiraḥ sarvā tā romaśā kṛdhi ||
english: That which is our field, and this body of mine, and the head of that spread-out one — make all of those hairy and abundant.

sanskrit: khe rathasya khe 'nasaḥ khe yugasya śatakrato | apālām indra triṣ pūtvy akṛṇoḥ sūryatvacam ||
english: Through the hole of the chariot, through the hole of the wagon, through the hole of the yoke, O Śatakratu — Apālā, O Indra, you purified three times, you made her sun-skinned.

sanskrit: divas pṛṣṭhe madhupṛcaḥ suparṇāḥ pañcāśat te bhuvanasya gopāḥ | ānujāvaram anu rakṣanta ugrā yeṣām indraṃ vīryāyairayanta ||
english: On the back of heaven, fifty honey-mixing suparṇas, guardians of the world — fierce, they protect rank by rank, those who stirred up Indra to heroic valor.

sanskrit: purohitaḥ parameṣṭhī svarājyāya- -abhīvardham asmā akṛṇod bṛhaspatiḥ | tena sapatnān adharān kṛṇuṣva kṣeme paśūn bahulān vardhayitvā jaitrāyod yātu rathavāhanaṃ te ||
english: The supreme chaplain Bṛhaspati made the abhīvardha-amulet for him for sovereignty. By means of it, lay your rivals low; having multiplied your cattle abundantly in peace, may your chariot-vehicle go forth to victory.

sanskrit: gobhājam aṃśaṃ tava ye samānāḥ sarve samagrā dadhṛg ābharanta | abhi vardhasva bhrātṛvyān abhi ye tvā pṛtanyataḥ ||
english: Those who are your peers, all of them together steadfastly brought along your share of cattle. Grow in power over your rivals, over those who make war on you.

sanskrit: ni piṇḍhi sarvān dhūrvato 'bhīvardho yathāsasi | abhīvardham abhībhavam abhīṣeṇaṃ mahāgaṇam | viśas tvā sarvā ā yantv āpo divyāḥ payasvatīḥ ||
english: Crush down all the injurers, be as the abhīvardha — the grower-in-superiority, the overcomer, the one with the overwhelming host. May all the clans come to you, may the heavenly, milk-laden waters come to you.

sanskrit: abhi vardhasva prajayā vāvṛdhāno abhy anīkaiḥ paśubhir bhavāsi | brahmarājanyair viśyair vāvṛdhānaḥ śūdrair atīhi sabhayā pṛtanyataḥ ||
english: Grow in power with offspring, waxing strong; may you prevail with armies and with cattle. Waxing strong with brāhmaṇas, rājanya warriors, and vaiśyas, with śūdras — overcome with your assembly those who make war on you.

sanskrit: vardhasva kṣetraiḥ prathasva prajayā vardhasva vīraiḥ paśubhir bahur bhava | śriyā śulkair yatamas tvā pṛtanyād āptas tubhyaṃ sa balihṛtyāya tiṣṭhatu ||
english: Grow in power with fields; spread wide with offspring; grow in power with heroes; become abundant with cattle. With glory and with tribute — whoever strives against you, let him, having been overcome, stand before you bringing tribute.
